issues.display_title: Issue #1400: Update Binary gtminity to Support PNG Images
issues.main_description_html:
Task Description

Update the gtminify binary to expand its image processing capabilities. The tool, which previously only supported the JPG format, is now being upgraded to fully support the PNG format as well.

Demo

🧪 QA Tester Results — Image Minifier (gtminify PNG support)

Tester: ekosy9 · Date: 2026-06-09 · Build: GoThru Photo Studio 1.0.84 Suite: qa_testing/e2e/edit/image_minifier.spec.ts (Playwright + Electron · PRO account · the Image Minifier driven through the real Edit module) · Automated result: 🟢 3 / 3 scenarios passed

✅ RESOLVED — "JPG minification process continues indefinitely even though the output file has been generated." Re-tested on build 1.0.84: the minify run now settles cleanly — the queue drains, the "All process completed" confirmation fires, and the output file is written to disk. The process no longer hangs after the output has been produced.

✅ PNG support confirmed (the core of #1400). gtminify now accepts PNG alongside JPG/JPEG — large PNGs (by file size and by pixel dimensions) and mixed PNG + JPG batches all minify with no "unsupported format" error and no failed items.

📝 Test summary

  • Scope: gtminify PNG support + the reported "infinite minify process after output is generated" bug, on GoThru Photo Studio 1.0.84 (PRO account).
  • Result: 🟢 3 / 3 automated scenarios passed.
  • PNG support: ✅ Large PNG (file size), large PNG (pixel dimensions), and mixed PNG + JPG batches all minified successfully — no unsupported-format error, no failed items.
  • Infinite-process bug: ✅ Fixed — each run now settles (queue drains + "All process completed" alert) and writes the output file; the process no longer continues indefinitely after the output is generated.
  • Output: ✅ A freshly-written minified file is produced on disk for every run.

Evidence hosted publicly in GoThruMedia/reports (video → user-attachments via reports#6; screenshots → issue-assets/1400/) so it renders both in the public report and inline on this issue — not only for repo members.
